text:
maya: nsys run from a prod replay shows sporadic cudaMalloc spikes during large-batch KV cache refills. spikes line up with host memcpy bursts and a 'createBuffer' kernel on the timeline. cc @ravi @liam

perf-bot: Perf artifact uploaded: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/1792004521 (nsys + perfetto) :rocket:

ravi: I noticed similar in canary last week. The spikes only appear once KV cache grows past ~1.8GB and when batching ramps up. Our arena uses 64MB chunk size by default — fragmentation seems to force fallback to direct cudaMalloc, which is expensive.

liam: nvprof/nsys snippets show kernel-selector switching to fallback kernels at those times. looks like allocation path blocks GPU work leading to CPU-side stalls. nsys capture excerpt:`bash
nsys profile --output=kv_alloc_trace ./serving_binary --replay id=20279
# timeline: createBuffer -> memcpy_h2d -> cudaMalloc -> memcpy_h2d -> kernel-x
`

sarah: Is this correlated with the batching heuristic change from last sprint? We bumped max_batch to 512 to improve throughput. Maybe distribution shifted so we get bigger, less frequent KV inserts. Those bursts could trigger many small allocations.

arun: I reproduced on dev with perfetto. Steps: `./run_infer --trace --kv-target 2G --max-batch 512 --seed 42`. Observed repeated pattern: many small frees then occasional big allocate that fails in arena and falls back. Perfetto slice: `cudaMalloc` spikes at ~200ms intervals, each spike corresponds to ~60-120ms stall. Proposed immediate mitigations: increase arena chunk size to 256MB and enable slab reuse policy for fragments <2MB.

maya: Patch idea seems reasonable. Let's also update kernel selection scoring so kernels that need temporary allocations get penalized. simple idea: add `memory_alloc_penalty = 1.2 * estimated_allocs` into the selector scoring function so we prefer lower-memory paths when SLOs matter.

liam: I'll prototype `eng-runtime:arena/tune-256` with chunk=256MB + slab reuse flag. Running a 24h soak with nsys capture and perf counters. also adding a new metric `alloc_scatter_count` to track how often arena returns fallback.

ravi: If we up chunk size, be careful about long-lived sessions and fragmentation over time. Suggest a periodic compaction/defrag pass that runs during idle windows or at low QPS, and a cap on how many chunks per arena we hold before triggering compaction.

sarah: :thumbsup: test plan: 1) run prototype on dev replay for 24h 2) validate tail latency and alloc_scatter_count 3) run canary with 1% traffic 4) capture nsys + perfetto for regression windows 5) roll out.

perf-bot: Benchmark job queued: perf/kv-alloc-soak #452 (nsys + perfetto). Results will post to the artifact link above.

maya: Thanks all — let's sync in tomorrow's standup. If soak passes, we can do a controlled canary. Also add an integration test to the perf matrix that exercises kv growth to 2.5GB so this doesn't regress.

liam: quick note on instrumentation: add counters for `arena_chunks_active`, `arena_free_frag_bytes`, `alloc_fallback_count`, and sample sizes of allocations when fallback occurs. that will help pinpoint thresholds.

arun: I'll attach the perfetto timeline screenshot to the artifact and drop the minimal repro script in the run folder. script uses synthetic KV inserts to reproduce fragmentation quickly.

maya: cool — assigning follow-ups: liam (proto + metrics), arun (repro + traces), ravi (compaction design), sarah (canary plan). ping me if soak shows any regressions.
